name: Nebraska
tagline: From Missouri River bluffs to Chimney Rock, by way of the Sandhills and the Pine Ridge.
intro: Nebraska's byways run the length of the state on old two-lane highways, following the Missouri River bluffs, the Platte and Loup valleys, the grass-covered dunes of the Sandhills and the buttes of the Panhandle. This chapter follows Nebraska's Scenic Byways as listed by the Nebraska Department of Transportation, which names nine routes and sends travelers to Visit Nebraska for details. Each byway is a single numbered highway, and two of them, the Lincoln Highway on US 30 and the Sandhills Journey on Highway 2, are also National Scenic Byways.

members.name: 385 - Gold Rush Byway
members.blurb: US 385 runs north from Sidney past Courthouse and Jail Rocks above Pumpkin Creek, then Carhenge outside Alliance, to the pine-covered buttes around Chadron, on a road that carried gold every day in the 1870s.

members.name: Bridges to Buttes Byway
members.blurb: US 20 runs west from Valentine across rolling Sandhills and northern prairie, past Cottonwood Lake at Merriman and the Pine Ridge around Chadron, to Harrison, with Toadstool Geologic Park's odd rock forms and fossil beds north of Crawford.

members.name: Heritage Highway
members.blurb: US 136 leaves the Missouri River at Brownville, a town of about 150, and runs west past Homestead National Historical Park at Beatrice to Red Cloud, where Willa Cather grew up, and on to Edison.

members.name: Lewis & Clark Scenic Byway
members.blurb: US 75 follows the Missouri River north from Omaha between cropland and wooded bluffs, past Fort Atkinson, once home to a quarter of the US Army, and across the Winnebago reservation to South Sioux City.

members.name: Lincoln Highway Scenic & Historic Byway
members.blurb: US 30 follows the old Lincoln Highway, the first coast-to-coast road, across the whole state from Blair to Kimball, by way of Grand Island, Kearney and North Platte, with a Pony Express station still standing in Gothenburg.

members.name: Loup Rivers Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Highways 11 and 91 follow the North Loup River from Wood River past red barns and silos, the Danish bakery at Dannebrog and the chalk mine at Scotia, then Fort Hartsuff and Calamus Reservoir, into the Sandhills at Dunning.

members.name: Outlaw Trail Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Highway 12 runs west from near South Sioux City by Lewis and Clark Lake and the Niobrara River bluffs to Valentine, passing Monowi, a town of one, and Smith Falls, the highest waterfall in Nebraska.

members.name: Sandhills Journey Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Highway 2 leaves Grand Island for the grass-covered dunes of the Sandhills, among the largest such dune fields in the world, passing the Nebraska National Forest and ranch towns like Mullen and Hyannis on the way to Alliance.

members.name: Western Trails Scenic & Historic Byway
members.blurb: From Ogallala and Lake McConaughy, US 26 and Highway 92 follow the North Platte valley on the line of the Oregon Trail, past Ash Hollow and Chimney Rock to the wagon ruts at Scotts Bluff.

sources.label: Nebraska Department of Transportation, Scenic Byways
